notes: KNEES ONLY (2 + 1 spare). Same 22.8x12.2 footprint as MG90S, +0.4g, ~45% more torque. Moves the mass budget from 205g to 245g -- cheaper than any airframe diet. PROVISIONAL SPEC: bench-measure before trusting.
6 used (hip roll x2, hip pitch x2, ankle x2) + 2 spare. Buy one lot; clones vary.
2 used (neck_pitch, head_yaw) + 1 spare. head_yaw is the binding joint at 76%.
Module, not a devkit: a devkit is 8g of USB connector and headers we do not need. No PSRAM because the policy is quantised to int8 (193KB) and lives in internal SRAM.
Carries the ESP32-S3-MINI, PCA9685, MCP3208, 6V BEC, IMU and the 10 pot dividers. One board instead of five breakouts saves ~15g and most of the wiring.
10 servos; ESP32-S3 LEDC has only 8 channels.
10 pot-tap channels needs 2. ADS1115 at 860 SPS is far too slow -- do not substitute.
Only gyro(3) + accel(3) are in the observation. MPU-6050 works for v1 if cost matters.
~19 min walking at ~1.5A. 850mAh is +20g and costs 4 points of joint margin -- see README 5.
Only if not integrating the BEC on the PCB. 5A is NOT enough: 8 servos stalling is ~5.6A.
Across the servo rail, at the board.
Pot dividers, 2 per channel. NOT lower: loading the 5k pot shifts the servo.
ADC anti-alias. NOT 1uF: 50ms time constant would break 50Hz control.
MG90S output shaft is single-sided; every joint needs an idler bearing opposite the horn.
~33g printed: trunk shell 10, 8 joint brackets 12, feet 7, head/neck 4. Building the geometry turned up brackets the first round-number estimate missed. PETG over PLA: the joints see real load.
Includes spares. Servo cost ~7300 JPY vs ~63000 for 14 XL330.
Matches sim/nanoduck.xml exactly -- the model is the authority on mass. Worst joint: knee at 62%, comfortably under the 76% MicroDuck's own knee runs at.
